sections.skill: Compare renting and owning and explain the parts of a mortgage

questions.prompt: What is a mortgage?

choices.text: A monthly rent payment to a landlord
Insurance that protects a home and its contents from fire
A loan to buy a home, with the home as collateral
A savings account for a down payment

questions.correct_answer: A loan to buy a home, with the home as collateral
questions.intro: A mortgage is a loan used to buy a home. The home is collateral: if the borrower does not repay, the lender can foreclose (take and sell the home). Mortgages usually last 15 or 30 years and are repaid with monthly payments of principal and interest.
questions.feedback: A mortgage is a home loan secured by the home.
questions.topic: Renting versus owning, and what a mortgage is
sources: CFPB (Buying a House): Mortgage payments often include principal, interest, property taxes, and homeowners insurance (PITI); private mortgage insurance is usually required with less than 20% down on a conventional loan. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/)

questions.prompt: The Lees buy a $300,000 home with a 20% down payment. How much do they borrow?
questions.intro: The down payment is the part of the price paid up front in cash. The rest is borrowed: loan (principal) = price − down payment.

questions.prompt: Which is an advantage of OWNING compared with renting?

choices.text: Payments can build equity (ownership) over time
It is easier to move on short notice when owning

questions.correct_answer: Payments can build equity (ownership) over time
questions.intro: Owning can build equity, the part of the home you own (value − mortgage balance), and gives stability and control. Renting offers flexibility and fewer responsibilities: landlords handle major repairs and you can move more easily.
questions.feedback: Equity grows as the loan is paid down and if the home rises in value.

sections.skill: The true cost of renting versus owning

questions.prompt: Rent is $1,800 a month. An owner's total monthly cost is $2,400 (mortgage, tax, insurance, upkeep), of which $500 is principal that builds equity. What is the owner's monthly cost NOT counting principal?
questions.intro: Part of a mortgage payment (principal) builds equity, which is like saving. Comparing renting and owning fairly separates costs that are spent from money that builds ownership.
questions.feedback: $2,400 − $500 = $1,900 of costs that do not build equity.

choices.text: Homes always lose value during their first two years

questions.feedback: Transaction costs are spread over few years, raising the yearly cost of owning.
